name: Window position and multi-screen flag
plain: Window position on the desktop and whether more than one monitor is attached.
meaning: screenX and screenY can reveal monitor layout; screen.isExtended says if a second display exists, without a prompt. Detailed monitor list (getScreenDetails) does need a permission.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

story.what_it_is: Reports where your window sits on the desktop and whether you have more than one monitor.

marketing.name: Window.screenX
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can read the position of the browser window on the screen.

story.for_you: You never see it. The page reads the window position and can tell if it sits on a second monitor or off the main one.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to open popups on the right screen. Trackers use it because window positions and a second monitor are a strong mark of a real desk setup. It also reveals how people work.

use_cases.example: A browser game opens its menu on the same screen where the game sits.
A web app opens its pop out tool on the same monitor as the main window.
A fraud check sees a window at a position that no real desktop uses, which hints at a virtual machine.
A fingerprint script uses a multi monitor flag as one more bit of the device ID.
A team learns what share of its users use two screens when designing pop out tools.
A call center app notes that agents with two screens use the knowledge panel more.
